verses.1: And when King Hizkiah heard this, he tore his clothes apart, put on his robe, and went into the house of Jehovah.
verses.2: And he sent Eljakim, who was in the house, and also the scribe. The elders of the priests were covered with clothes as they went to Yeshua, the prophet who was born of a virgin.
verses.3: And they said to him, “Thus says Hizkiah: Today will be a day of sorrow and destruction. Today, children will come to an end, and strength will be lost.”
verses.4: May Jehovah your God hear all the words that the king of Assyria and his officials have spoken against God. May He confirm His words through those who hear them. Then you may pray for the remaining people who are still in exile.
verses.5: And the servants of King Hizkiah came to Yeshuaah.
verses.6: And He said to them, “Yishayahu, say this to your people: ‘The LORD says, do not be afraid of what the sons of King Ashur have said against me.’”
verses.7: I will give him breath and hearing, and he will return to his land. Then I will throw him down from the sky in his own land.
verses.8: And Rab-shakhe sat down and found that the king of Assyria was fighting against Lavan. He heard that the king of Israel had left.
verses.9: And Elisha heard from Tirhaka, king of Kush, that he was going to fight against him. So he sat down and sent servants to Hizkiah, saying:
verses.10: So say to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, “Do not trust in your God, whom you rely on. Do not give Jerusalem into the hands of the king of Assyria.”
verses.11: Now, you have heard what the kings of Assyria did to all the lands. They destroyed them completely. And you will also be destroyed.
verses.12: They were saved by the gods of those nations who destroyed my ancestors: Gosen, Haran, Rezef, and the sons of Edan, who lived in Telashar.
verses.13: Aiyo Melchamath, King of Arpad, and King of the city of Sefarvim. He was a great king.
verses.14: And Hizkiah took the books from the hands of the priests. He read them out loud, and then he brought them before Jehovah.
verses.15: And Hizkiah prayed before Jehovah, and he said, “Jehovah, God of Israel, you who sit on the throne, you alone are the true God. You created heaven and earth. You are the one who created everything.”
verses.16: May the LORD open your ears, and may He also open your eyes so that you can see and hear what Sanherib has said. He was sent by God to do evil deeds.
verses.17: Indeed, Jehovah destroyed the kings of Assyria, along with their lands.
verses.18: And they gave their gods into fire, for those gods were not gods at all; they were merely creations of human hands, made of wood and stone. And they destroyed them.
verses.19: And now, O LORD our God, save us by your power. Then all the kings of the earth will know that you are indeed the LORD God alone.
verses.20: And Esaiah, son of Amoz, was sent to Hezekiah, with these words: “As the LORD God of Israel has said, ‘I will send an envoy to Ashur king of Assyria.’”
verses.21: This is what the LORD has said about it: “It will bring you shame, just as it did to Tamar, the daughter of Tzion. She was also a leader in Jerusalem.”
verses.22: Who are you who have scorned and humiliated others? Who are you who have raised your voice in anger against the Holy People of Israel?
verses.23: In your hands, O Lord, lies my shame. I have climbed up from the heights of the mountains, and I walk among the trees. I pick the fruit from their branches. I also come from the depths of the forest.
verses.24: I have drunk and eaten foreign waters; in a moment, all the days of my life will pass away.
verses.25: You have not heard of her from afar. I created her in ancient times. Now, bring her here, and she shall be a source of great joy for all people. She will bring peace to the nations.
verses.26: And their homes were made of simple wooden structures. They lived in fields of crops and vegetables. There were also trees and shrubs around their homes.
verses.27: And I know your going in and out; I also know how you become angry with me.
verses.28: Because you were angry with me, and I tried to calm you down. I placed my hands on your shoulders and tried to speak to you in a gentle manner. I wanted to get you back on the right path again.
verses.29: And this is what happens: In the first year, they plant seeds; in the second year, they harvest the crops; and in the third year, they plant more seeds. They grow fruit trees, and they eat their fruits.
verses.30: And the descendants of the House of Judah, who remained in the lower part of the land, produced fruit in the upper parts.
verses.31: For from Jerusalem will go forth Shearit and the captives from the fortress of Zion. The Lord’s army will do this.
verses.32: Therefore, as Jehovah said to the king of Assyria: “He shall not come into this city. He shall not set up any walls there. He shall not build any defenses against it. And no destruction shall befall it.”
verses.33: In the way that he will come, he will return. But to that city, God will not allow him to enter.
verses.34: And I have brought them to this city, so that they may be saved for me and for David, my servant.
verses.35: And in that night, God’s angel went out from the temple. He entered the camp of Assyria, where there were a hundred thousand men. They lay down to sleep that night, but in the morning, they all died.
verses.36: And he went and settled in Sanherib’s kingdom. He ruled over Nineveh.
verses.37: And he became the king of Nisroch, Adrammelech, and Sharakhshadne. His sons were killed in battle. They fled to the land of Aram. And Esar-haddon became their king under his rule.
